allowedSourceMaterial.overview: A reporter becomes the target of a vicious smear campaign that drives him to the point of suicide after he exposes the CIA's role in arming Contra rebels in Nicaragua and importing cocaine into California. Based on the true story of journalist Gary Webb.

facts.overview: A reporter becomes the target of a vicious smear campaign that drives him to the point of suicide after he exposes the CIA's role in arming Contra rebels in Nicaragua and importing cocaine into California. Based on the true story of journalist Gary Webb.
facts.title: Kill the Messenger

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: When an intrepid reporter traces an illicit pipeline back to the federal government, the blowback threatens to destroy his life.
visibleEditorialCopy.description: Based on a true story, journalist Gary Webb uncovers ties between the CIA, Nicaraguan Contra rebels, and crack cocaine entering California, triggering a ferocious smear campaign against him.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: A somber, suspenseful true-crime political drama requiring engaged focus for an emotionally heavy solo watch.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: Director Michael Cuesta crafts a tense, thoughtful procedural exploring the punishing personal costs of investigative reporting and institutional retaliation.

claudeAdvisory.sourceBoundaryReason: Every concrete claim (Gary Webb, the CIA and Contra rebels, cocaine entering California, the smear campaign, the true-story basis, the director, the genres) is grounded in the authorized overview. The remaining language ('intrepid', 'illicit pipeline', 'blowback', 'procedural', 'punishing personal costs') is figurative characterization or genre shorthand. None of it functions as a meaningful new factual claim about plot mechanics, identities, relationships, motives or causality under A_PRIME_PRODUCTION_MATERIALITY_V1. The copy also declines to state the overview's suicide detail, so no spoiler-boundary content appears.

sourceEvidence.notes: description: the true-story basis, journalist Gary Webb, the CIA, the Nicaraguan Contra rebels, cocaine entering California, and the resulting smear campaign all restate the overview. 'Engaged focus' matches attentionDemand=engaged. 'Solo watch' matches situations=[alone]. Keyword-only material (San Jose, homicide-style details, drug dealer material) is not imported.

claudeAdvisory.uncertaintyNotes: Two items sit near the tolerance line. 'Crack cocaine' specifies a form of cocaine that appears only in facts.keywords ('crack cocaine'), while the overview says only 'cocaine' and allowedSourceMaterial.keywords is empty. It is a small concretization that does not change what a viewer would expect, so I kept it within tolerance. A stricter closed-world reading could ask for 'cocaine' to be restored, in which case it would be a MINOR factual concretization. 'Procedural' in whyWatch implies an investigative-process structure that the overview only loosely supports, and I left it within tolerance as genre shorthand.

geminiAdvisory.sourceBoundaryReason: All visible editorial copy strictly complies with A_PRIME_PRODUCTION_MATERIALITY_V1. The narrative premise, investigative conflict, and institutional backlash in the description and curiosityHook faithfully reflect the authorized overview and verified keywords. Crucially, the copy exercises disciplined setup-only restraint: it refrains from detailing the protagonist's eventual suicide or third-act tragic revelations mentioned in the overview, framing the stakes neutrally as personal blowback and retaliation. Tonal descriptors such as 'illicit pipeline' and 'institutional retaliation' operate as legitimate, low-risk contextual concretization and genre shorthand cleanly anchored in the verified facts and semantic classifications.
